text_blocks.snippet: In the United States, asylum is a form of protection granted to foreign nationals who are already in the country or arriving at a port of entry, and who are unable or unwilling to return to their home country due to persecution or a well-founded fear of persecution on account of their race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership in a particular social group. This right is enshrined in international and US law, and individuals seeking asylum must demonstrate a credible fear of persecution to be eligible.
